newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform goes to a vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform goes to a vote.

text.p: Reform of Brazil's civil service rules was due to be put before the Chamber of Deputies later on Wednesday, Congress officials said.
The officials said the civil service bill was the 17th item on the agenda. The session was to start at 1400 local/1700 GMT.
A spokeswoman for chief whip Benito Gama said the government expected the vote to proceed without further delay.
"They will vote today," she said, adding that political leaders had agreed to present the original reform proposal, including a public sector salary ceiling equivalent to 10,800 reais a month.
"They (the deputies) may well present amendments but as it stands, they will vote on the original proposal including the salary ceiling," the spokeswoman said.
Newspapers reported that President Fernando Henrique Cardoso had threatened to fire up to 50,000 public sector servants if deputies failed to vote Wednesday.
Presidency officials and aides to government leaders in Congress said they could not confirm the reports.

They noted that it would have been out of character for Cardoso to threaten Congress but added he may well have presented the mass redundancy as the "unavoidable consequence" if Congress failed to pass the reform.
The vote has been held up amid bickering over the salary ceiling. At least 140 deputies earn more than the proposed limit and do not relish the prospect of voting themselves a pay cut.
Civil service reform is considered a necessary tool to control public spending and help Brazil narrow its gaping public sector fiscal deficit.

Many states spend more than 60 percent of their receipts just on payroll and pensions and are unable to reduce the burden because of constitutional job guarantees. The 50,000 civil servants Cardoso reportedly threatened to dismiss hold positions not protected by constitutional rights.
As a constitutional amendment, the bill must be approved twice in both the lower and upper hosues, each time with a three-fifths majority.
